## Analysis

**Setup.** $X = (X_*)^*$ is a dual Banach space. The weak\* topology of $B(X)$ is the topology of pointwise convergence on $X$ (with $\sigma(X,X_*)$): a net $T_\alpha \to T$ iff $\varphi(T_\alpha x) \to \varphi(Tx)$ for all $x \in X$, $\varphi \in X_*$.

**Characterization of $B_{w^*}(X)$.** An operator $T \in B(X)$ is $w^*$-continuous (continuous $\sigma(X,X_*)\to\sigma(X,X_*)$) iff for every $\varphi \in X_*$, the functional $\varphi\circ T$ is $\sigma(X,X_*)$-continuous, i.e., $\varphi\circ T \in X_*$. Equivalently, $T^*(X_*)\subseteq X_*$, where $T^*:X^*\to X^*$ is the adjoint and $X^*=(X_*)^{**}$.

So $B_{w^*}(X)=\{T\in B(X): T^*(X_*)\subseteq X_*\}$.

---

## Proof

**Claim:** $B_{w^*}(X)$ is closed in the weak\* topology of $B(X)$ **if and only if** $X$ is reflexive (equivalently $X_*$ is reflexive). In particular, for a general dual Banach space, $B_{w^*}(X)$ is **not** closed.

### ($\Leftarrow$) If $X$ is reflexive, $B_{w^*}(X)=B(X)$.

If $X_*$ is reflexive, then $X^*=(X_*)^{**}=X_*$, so $T^*(X_*)\subseteq X^*=X_*$ automatically for every $T\in B(X)$. Hence $B_{w^*}(X)=B(X)$, which is trivially closed. $\checkmark$

### ($\Rightarrow$) If $X_*$ is **not** reflexive, $B_{w^*}(X)$ is **not** closed.

Since $X_*$ is not reflexive, $X_*\subsetneq (X_*)^{**}=X^*$, so there exists a nonzero $\psi\in X^*\setminus X_*$. Scale so that $\|\psi\|\leq 1$; since $X_*$ is a linear subspace, $\psi\notin X_*$ still holds.

By **Goldstine's theorem**, the unit ball of $X_*$ is $\sigma((X_*)^{**},(X_*)^*)$-dense in the unit ball of $(X_*)^{**}=X^*$. Since $(X_*)^*=X$, this is the $\sigma(X^*,X)$-topology, i.e., pointwise convergence on $X$. Therefore there exists a net $(\psi_\alpha)$ in the unit ball of $X_*$ with
$$\psi_\alpha(x)\to\psi(x)\quad\text{for all }x\in X.$$

Pick $x_0\in X\setminus\{0\}$ (so $x_0\neq 0$). Since $X_*$ separates points of $X=(X_*)^*$, there is $\varphi_0\in X_*$ with $\varphi_0(x_0)\neq 0$.

Define rank-one operators:
$$T_\alpha x := \psi_\alpha(x)\cdot x_0,\qquad Tx:=\psi(x)\cdot x_0.$$

**Each $T_\alpha\in B_{w^*}(X)$:** We have $(T_\alpha)^*\varphi = \varphi(x_0)\,\psi_\alpha\in X_*$ for every $\varphi\in X_*$ (since $\psi_\alpha\in X_*$). So $T_\alpha^*(X_*)\subseteq X_*$. Also $\|T_\alpha\|=\|x_0\|\|\psi_\alpha\|\leq\|x_0\|<\infty$, so $T_\alpha\in B(X)$. $\checkmark$

**$T_\alpha\to T$ in the weak\* topology of $B(X)$:** For any $x\in X$, $\varphi\in X_*$:
$$\varphi(T_\alpha x)=\varphi\big(\psi_\alpha(x)\,x_0\big)=\psi_\alpha(x)\,\varphi(x_0)\longrightarrow \psi(x)\,\varphi(x_0)=\varphi(Tx).$$
$\checkmark$

**$T\notin B_{w^*}(X)$:** We have $T^*\varphi_0 = \varphi_0(x_0)\,\psi$. Since $\varphi_0(x_0)\neq 0$ and $\psi\notin X_*$ (and $X_*$ is a linear subspace), $T^*\varphi_0\notin X_*$. Hence $T^*(X_*)\not\subseteq X_*$, so $T\notin B_{w^*}(X)$. $\checkmark$

We have produced a net in $B_{w^*}(X)$ converging (in the weak\* topology of $B(X)$) to an operator outside $B_{w^*}(X)$. Therefore $B_{w^*}(X)$ is **not closed**.

---

## Conclusion

$B_{w^*}(X)$ is closed in the weak\* topology of $B(X)$ **if and only if $X$ is reflexive**. For a general (non-reflexive) dual Banach space, $B_{w^*}(X)$ is **not** a closed subset. The key mechanism is Goldstine's theorem: when $X_*$ is non-reflexive, $X_*$ is a proper weak\*-dense (hence non-closed) subspace of $X^*=(X_*)^{**}$, and rank-one operators built from approximating nets expose this non-closedness inside $B(X)$.
